topics.title: CutBrief
topics.label: Retired prototype · historical notes
topics.answer: CutBrief is retired. Its historical supplied-media prototype combined editable shot plans, actor and location references, trimming, captions and stitched exports. Robert previously reported a submission, but no contest result is claimed. Earlier public workspace links are historical, not a current supported download. Paid scene and video generation remain locked. It is separate from the personal Video Studio.

details.answer: The retired CutBrief prototype connected a written shot plan to supplied media, references, trimming, captions and stitched exports. These are historical prototype notes, not an actively supported release. Paid generation remains locked.

how.answer: Historically, CutBrief used a written shot plan and supplied media, followed by human review of takes, timing, captions and the assembled result. CutBrief is now retired; these notes are not current setup instructions.

status.answer: CutBrief is retired. Its historical supplied-media prototype combined editable shot plans, actor and location references, trimming, captions and stitched exports. Robert previously reported a submission, but no contest result is claimed. Earlier public workspace links are historical, not a current supported download. cost.answer: CutBrief is retired. The historical supplied-media path needed no paid generation credits, but paid scene and video generation remain locked.

privacy.answer: The available CutBrief notes do not establish a complete policy for uploaded-media retention or sharing. A public workspace link is not a privacy guarantee. Check the workspace’s current information before supplying sensitive material.

voice.answer: CutBrief’s supplied-media workflow can use your own media in an assembled export. The reviewed notes do not establish a released automatic voice or lip-sync generation service. The Sarah read-aloud voice on this website is separate.

limits.answer: CutBrief is retired. Its historical tests do not establish a supported current service, successful hosted generation or an automatic finished-movie workflow. Paid generation remains locked.

topics.title: ShiftBrief
topics.label: Free Windows release · reviewed September 12, 2026
topics.answer: ShiftBrief is a free Windows business workspace for small teams. It brings employee availability, opening hours, schedules, completed-work records and source notes into one place. Sarah can answer from exact saved records and prepare staffing or coverage options for human review. Records · offline needs no AI model or account. The Windows installer includes the runtime; optional AI setup is separate. Start with a blank business or explicitly load the fictional eight-person demo.
next: How do I save and move my business?
What happens when an employee quits?

status.answer: Download the free ShiftBrief 0.1.0 Windows installer, run it and follow the setup prompts. The installer includes the Python runtime and app dependencies, so no separate Python setup is needed. A desktop shortcut is optional. Open ShiftBrief to use its local browser interface. Uninstalling the app retains saved business data. The public source checkout is also available; its manual Python setup is separate from the installer.

install.answer: Download the free ShiftBrief 0.1.0 Windows installer, run it and follow the setup prompts. The installer includes the Python runtime and app dependencies, so no separate Python setup is needed. A desktop shortcut is optional. Open ShiftBrief to use its local browser interface. Uninstalling the app retains saved business data. The public source checkout is also available; its manual Python setup is separate from the installer.

cost.answer: ShiftBrief is free to download and use. Records · offline requires no account, model or usage credits. Optional cloud AI uses your own provider access and may cost money; optional local AI needs a separately installed model.

first_run.answer: A first-time workspace starts with a blank business. You can create your own business, choose Load saved business, restore a complete backup from another computer, or explicitly Load demo. The optional Maple Street example is fictional: eight invented employees and sample records. It is not loaded automatically. Keep demo work separate from your own business and select the business you intend to edit.

save.answer:
Use Save business copy to download the selected business as a .shiftbrief.json file. On another computer, choose Load saved business to add it without removing businesses already there. The copy includes employees and history, availability, operating settings, planned schedules and recorded work. It excludes documents and conversations; use the complete backup for those.

Use Back up all businesses for a complete .shiftbrief-workspace.json backup, including all businesses, documents and extracted revisions, handoffs and conversations. On the other computer choose Restore backup from previous computer, review the summary and confirm. Restore replaces that computer’s workspace after saving a backup of its previous state. Linked external documents stay disabled until you choose their paths again. Copy external original files separately; the backup does not include the app, models or credentials.

how.answer:
In Records · offline, Sarah uses supported questions and saved-record tools, not a general language model. You can prepare employee and availability forms, inspect planned and completed work, review weekly schedules, lunch and sick-call options, and find source-backed notes. Draft proposals require review and acceptance before they become saved schedules. Unknown availability is not invented, and asking a question does not send a message to employees.

ShiftBrief keeps employee records, dated availability, business hours, saved schedules and recorded work together. Sarah helps answer exact-record questions, prepare staffing drafts and inspect uncovered time, so you can compare options without reconstructing the facts from scattered notes. Its saved revisions and review steps make it easier to see what was proposed and what you accepted. It does not promise a particular time saving or staffing outcome.

benefits.answer: ShiftBrief keeps employee records, dated availability, business hours, saved schedules and recorded work together. Sarah helps answer exact-record questions, prepare staffing drafts and inspect uncovered time, so you can compare options without reconstructing the facts from scattered notes. Its saved revisions and review steps make it easier to see what was proposed and what you accepted. It does not promise a particular time saving or staffing outcome.

technical.answer: Records · offline works without an installed AI model, account, API key or usage credits. Optional AI · local Ollama uses a separately installed and configured local model; no model weights are bundled. Optional AI · cloud Bedrock requires your own configured AWS access and can incur provider charges. Cloud use sends the question, recent conversation and selected saved facts to that provider. Choosing an AI mode does not authorize schedule changes or employee contact.

ai.answer: Records · offline works without an installed AI model, account, API key or usage credits. Optional AI · local Ollama uses a separately installed and configured local model; no model weights are bundled. Optional AI · cloud Bedrock requires your own configured AWS access and can incur provider charges. Cloud use sends the question, recent conversation and selected saved facts to that provider. Choosing an AI mode does not authorize schedule changes or employee contact.

departures.answer: If you report an already-decided departure, such as “I fired Morgan Stone” or “Morgan Stone quit,” Sarah opens an employment-ending review. You enter or review the first unavailable date; the chat message alone does not change it. Preview remaining shifts reads saved schedules without saving the departure. After you explicitly record the date, the coverage review totals remaining saved shifts and net planned hours and suggests eligible off-schedule people or adjacent early-start/late-finish options. It checks saved qualifications, availability, time off, overlap, employment dates and weekly restrictions. These are independent alternatives for your review, not a combined reassignment plan or confirmation that anyone agreed. Earlier history stays intact, and Sarah does not decide whom to fire.

privacy.answer: The installed app saves its workspace on your computer. Records · offline uses local saved records. Business copies and complete backups are files you choose to share or move; keep them somewhere you trust. Optional cloud AI sends selected context to the configured provider. The website guide is separate: it has no access to your installed businesses and does not send this chat to Robert.

details.answer:
In Records · offline, Sarah uses supported questions and saved-record tools, not a general language model. You can prepare employee and availability forms, inspect planned and completed work, review weekly schedules, lunch and sick-call options, and find source-backed notes. Draft proposals require review and acceptance before they become saved schedules. Unknown availability is not invented, and asking a question does not send a message to employees.

A first-time workspace starts with a blank business. You can create your own business, choose Load saved business, restore a complete backup from another computer, or explicitly Load demo. The optional Maple Street example is fictional: eight invented employees and sample records. It is not loaded automatically. Keep demo work separate from your own business and select the business you intend to edit.

voice.answer: The website’s Voice on button uses browser or device read-aloud. That is separate from ShiftBrief’s text workflow. The Windows installer does not include a personal voice model. Records · offline works through text without voice setup.

limits.answer: ShiftBrief is an early desktop release. Coverage options depend on the dates, availability, qualifications and restrictions you saved; missing records are not guessed. Planned hours are not proof of attendance or payroll. It is not payroll software or a labor-law assessment, and it does not contact employees, choose whom to fire or automatically assign replacement shifts. Website Sarah only explains these published notes and cannot open or change your desktop businesses.

topics.title: ClearTrail
topics.label: Prototype notes · September 7, 2026
topics.answer: ClearTrail helps office, home, research and community projects keep evidence behind a decision. Import text or readable PDFs, retain revisions, compare exact changes and ask Sarah for matching source passages. Saved briefings keep their quotes and can be exported; older briefings are marked when the evidence changes. Possible disagreements remain for review, and a newer record is not automatically approved. The default written workflow is bounded retrieval and comparison, not a general language model. The browser prototype requires no installed model, API key or credits and remains in private owner review. It is not connected to an Alexa device and has no announced public access link.
next: Can I try the prototypes today?

topics.title: Carry On
topics.label: Prototype notes · September 7, 2026
topics.answer: Carry On organizes work, home, travel and other plans into tasks, dependencies and readiness checks. Written Sarah can help develop a plan and propose changes; reviewed confirmations apply supported changes while preserving task IDs and history. Dependency cycles and stale edits are rejected. The browser prototype saves work in this browser and supports real export, backup and restore. Its bounded planning core needs no installed model, API key, voice folder or usage credits. It is in private owner review, with no public judge-access link announced. Carry On does not book travel, send messages or run a connected Alexa assistant.

How are Carry On plans saved?

topics.title: Kira Sequence Desk
topics.label: Prototype notes · September 7, 2026
topics.answer: Kira Sequence Desk is the smaller browser sequence-planning prototype for the AI Builders work. Turn your notes into timed, source-linked steps; revise wording, order and timing; attach your own images, audio or video; and review coverage gaps. Written approval applies to the exact plan and clears after edits. Export produces an editable ZIP with the plan, source map, review issues and selected original media. It does not render a finished movie or generate new footage. Written Sarah uses a bounded source planner, not a general language model, and requires no model, API key, account or voice installation. Work stays in browser storage with backup and restore. This is in private owner review, separate from the full personal Video Studio, with no public access link announced.

topics.label: Project notes · September 12, 2026

ClearTrail keeps evidence behind decisions, Carry On organizes tasks and readiness, and Kira Sequence Desk prepares timed, source-linked media plans; those three remain private owner-review prototypes in these notes. CutBrief is retired, with its prior submission preserved as history and paid generation locked. The personal Video Studio is a separate project still under development. No contest result is claimed.
